facts.content: Patient has had a sore throat for one week, which led to a dry cough.
The cough is dry with no sputum or hemoptysis and not worse at night.
facts.source_text: Dry, no sputum/hemoptysis; not worse at night

facts.content: The patient has shortness of breath for 3-4 days, only on exertion, and mild wheeze with vague chest pain.
facts.source_text: SOB x3-4 d, only on exertion; mild wheeze, vague chest pain

facts.content: Fever was present for the first three days and then resolved, with intermittent headaches.
The patient's appetite has decreased slightly, but there is no weight loss.
The course of the illness fluctuates, and the patient missed two workdays.
The patient denies any nasal congestion or rashes.
The patient has no past medical or surgical history.
The patient is not currently taking any medication.
The patient is allergic to peanuts.
The patient's mother has had lung cancer, and there are no instances of venous thromboembolism in the family.
facts.source_text: FH: mother lung CA; no VTE

facts.content: The patient is a non-smoker with minimal past experimentation, is a UK resident born in the US, and has recently traveled only within Europe.
facts.source_text: SH: non-smoker (minimal past experimentation); UK resident, born US; recent travel only within Europe

facts.content: The patient has no known asbestos exposure.
The patient likely has viral pharyngitis/bronchitis with resolving fever and dry cough.
facts.source_text: 1. Viral pharyngitis/bronchitis with resolving fever, dry cough

facts.content: There is possible mild reactive airway component indicated by a wheeze.
The patient has health anxiety regarding tuberculosis and lung cancer.
Occupational consideration: requires fit note.
Educate and reassure, indicating low likelihood of tuberculosis or malignancy.
facts.source_text: Education/reassurance: low likelihood TB or malignancy

facts.content: Symptomatic treatment includes paracetamol as needed, fluids, and rest.
facts.source_text: Symptomatic Tx: paracetamol PRN, fluids, rest

facts.content: Follow-up is advised if there is increased shortness of breath, new or worse chest pain, or persistent or worsening symptoms for more than 4-5 days.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: if ↑SOB, new/worse chest pain, persistent or worsening sx >4-5 d → face-to-face GP review

facts.content: The patient will receive a sick note for additional work absence.
facts.source_text: Provide sick note for additional work absence

facts.content: Safety-net advice was reiterated.
